newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ATHLETICS-OLYMPIC CHAMPION THUGWANE ATTACKED FOR A SECOND TIME.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-OLYMPIC CHAMPION THUGWANE ATTACKED FOR A SECOND TIME.

text.p: Josia Thugwane, the first black South African to win an Olympic gold medal, was assaulted by an irate motorist at the same spot where three car hijackers shot him five months ago.

The Star newspaper reported that Thugwane, surprise winner of the Atlanta Olympics marathon, was on his way home after training on Thursday when he almost collided with an oncoming car while overtaking a truck.
The outraged driver pulled the diminutive Thugwane from his car and punched him in the mouth.
He was treated at a local hospital for shock, bruises and a cut to his mouth.
The assault meant Thugwane was forced to miss one of the country's most prestigious sports awards ceremonies on Thursday night where he was named South Africa's most outstanding sportsperson of 1996.
Thugwane's first major appearance since his win in Atlanta will come in the London marathon on April 13.

Confirming his entry on Friday, race co-ordinator Dave Bedford said: "Given the nature of the London course I believe Thugwane could pose a real threat to the longstanding record of two hours eight minutes 16 seconds."
